result.summary: Roman envoys led by Orestes announce that Sparta, Corinth, Argos and other cities should be released from the Achaean League. The Achaeans react with violence against Spartans, send embassies, and under the new General Critolaus deceive the Roman commissioners and march to war, encouraged by Thebes.

scenes.title: Orestes' announcement and the riot
scenes.summary: Orestes tells the Achaean leaders that Rome would free several cities from the League. The Achaeans attack and then imprison Spartans at Corinth despite Orestes' protests.
scenes.stakes: The Achaeans risk Roman anger and the loss of cities from their League.

scenes.title: Critolaus deceives the Romans
scenes.summary: Achaean ambassadors go to Rome but turn back on meeting later envoys. Critolaus, the new General, tricks the Roman commissioners at Tegea and then raises an army at Corinth for war.
scenes.stakes: Critolaus gambles the whole Achaean League on war with Rome.

scenes.title: Reflection and Theban eagerness
scenes.summary: Pausanias comments that reckless war is madness, not bad luck. Pytheas and the Thebans, resentful of fines imposed by Metellus, join the cause.
scenes.stakes: Thebes risks ruin by joining a hopeless war.

notable_quotes.reason: Pausanias judges the Achaean war as madness rather than bad luck.

analysis.text: Pausanias blames the Achaean disaster on reckless folly rather than fate, a moral judgement on leaders who ignored their weakness.
The passage describes the build-up to the Achaean War of 146 BC, which ended with Rome's destruction of Corinth and its control of Greece.

language_notes.text: "_viz._" abbreviates the Latin videlicet, "namely"; it introduces the list of cities Rome would detach from the League.
Spartans were identified by hairstyle, boots and dress; Spartan men traditionally wore their hair long, so appearance served as a marker of identity.
"Ostensibly" means apparently or for show; Critolaus's stated purpose hid his real aim of avoiding a general assembly.
"Guile" means cunning deceit; here a false appeal to procedure delays the Romans.
Bœotarch was the title of the chief magistrates of the Boeotian federation, of which Thebes was the leading city.

context_notes.text: Orestes was a Roman envoy; the Romans were arbitrating the dispute between the Spartans and the Achaean League.
The Achaean League was a federation of Peloponnesian cities. Rome wanted to loosen it by detaching members that had joined later.
Metellus was the Roman commander who defeated the Achaeans' allies in the war; his arbitration fined Thebes for attacks on neighbours.

literary_notes.text: Critolaus is drawn as passionate and duplicitous, publicly asking for a meeting while privately sabotaging it.
Madness is set against mere bad luck, so that responsibility falls on the Achaeans' own choices rather than on fate.
The brief remark about ruin prepares the reader for the Achaean defeat that follows.
